findings.title: Conflicting crypto providers are now silently picked instead of failing
findings.body: The old check threw "Multiple crypto providers loaded" when more than one provider was on the classpath. It is removed and replaced by sorting on `order()`. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200. A misconfigured classpath, such as default plus FIPS or default plus Elytron, now picks one by `ServiceLoader` order, which depends on classpath order. The rest are only mentioned at debug level. Before, this was a hard failure; now a FIPS deployment could silently run on the non-FIPS provider. Equal-order conflicts should still throw, or at least be logged at warn. Only the authz-client fallback (order 100) should be allowed to lose to another provider.

findings.title: New abstract `order()` method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: `order()` is added as an abstract interface method. Any external or custom `CryptoProvider` implementation, such as third-party or testsuite providers, will no longer compile. Already-compiled ones will fail with `AbstractMethodError` inside the `sorted(Comparator.comparingInt(CryptoProvider::order))` call in `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider`. A `default int order() { return 0; }` would keep source and binary compatibility.

findings.title: Dead duplicate encoder calls in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
findings.body: `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and the same for `sBigInteger` encode the values and discard the result. They have no effect, and the values are encoded again in the `writeDerSeq` call below. Remove them. The method also does not validate that `signature` has at least `signLength` bytes. A short, attacker-supplied JWS signature produces an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of an `IOException`.

findings.title: Indefinite or oversized length leads to unchecked exceptions or unbounded allocation
findings.body: `readLength()` returns -1 for the indefinite-length form (0x80). `readInteger()` then calls `read(length)` with -1, which throws `NegativeArraySizeException` instead of `IOException`. The `length >= limit` bounds check applies only to the long form. Short-form lengths are bounded by 127, but `read(int)` does not otherwise validate against the remaining input. Malformed DER input should be rejected with `IOException`. Reject negative lengths in `readInteger`/`readNext` and check the length against `is.available()`.

findings.title: Round-trip test never validates the DER encoder independently
findings.body: The test only checks that decode(encode(decode(x))) equals decode(x). It never verifies that the DER produced by `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` is accepted by a real JDK `Signature.verify`, and it never covers edge cases. Those edge cases include r/s with the high bit set, r/s shorter than the curve length (leading zeros), and malformed or indefinite-length input. A round trip with a symmetric bug would still pass. Compare the encoder output against the original JDK-produced DER and verify the signature with it.
